parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Thanks to all of you for coming along today to hear about how the robotic float project is helping with ocean research. Well, first of all we'll look at what a robotic float does and its use. So let's start with the device itself. It looks a bit like a cigar and it's about one and a half metres long. More importantly it's full of equipment that's designed to collect data. So, it can help us in building up a profile of different factors which work together within the world's oceans.

Sounds like a big project - isn't it too big for one country to undertake?

That's quite true but this project is a really good example of international cooperation. Over the last five years scientists from thirteen countries have been taking part in the project and launching floats in their area of ocean patrol. And next year this number will rise to fourteen when Indonesia joins the project.

That's impressive.

But let's move onto how floats work. The operational cycle goes like this. Each of the floats is dropped in the ocean from a boat at a set point and activated from a satellite. Then the float immediately sinks about 2,000 metres... that's two whole kilometres down in the water. It stays at this depth for about 10 days and is carried around by the currents which operate in the ocean at this level. During this time it's possible for it to cover quite large distances but the average is fifty kilometres.

So what is it actually recording?

Well at this stage nothing, but as it rises to the surface it collects all sorts of data, most importantly variations in salinity, that's salt levels, and the changes in temperature, a bit like underwater weather balloons. Then when it gets back to the surface all the data it's collected is beamed up to the satellite. After about five hours on the surface the float automatically sinks, beginning the whole process again.

What happens to the data?

Well the information is transferred direct to onshore meteorological stations... like our one in Hobart... and within four hours the findings can be on computers and they can be mapped and analysed.

You say you're building models of the world's ocean systems but how are they going to be used, and more importantly, when?

Some of the data has already helped in completing projects. For example, our understanding of the underlying causes of El Nino events is being confirmed by float data. Another way we're using float data is to help us to understand the mechanics of climate change, like global warming and ozone depletion. That's part of an ongoing variability study but the results are still a long way off. However, this is not the case with our ocean weather forecasting. Because we know from the floats what the prevailing weather conditions will be in certain parts of the ocean, we can advise the Navy on search and rescue missions. That's happening right now and many yachtsmen owe their lives to the success of this project. In addition, the float data can help us to look at the biological implications of ocean processes.

Would that help with preserving fish stocks?

Yes, and advising governments on fisheries legislation. We're well on the way to completing a project on this. We hope it will help to bring about more sustainable fishing practices. We'll be seeing the results of that quite soon.

It sounds like the data from floats has lots of applications.

Yes it does. It's also a powerful agricultural tool. If we were aware of what the weather would be like, say, next year, we could make sure that the farmers planted appropriate grain varieties to produce the best yield from the available rainfall.

That sounds a bit like science fiction, especially when now we can't even tell them when a drought will break.

I agree that this concept is still a long way in the future, but it will come eventually and the float data will have made a contribution.

analyses.content: 演讲者描述该设备的形状看起来有点像一根雪茄（cigar）。
Speaker: So let's start with the device itself. It looks a bit like a cigar and it's about one and a half metres long.
"It looks a bit like a..." 直接对应 "Float is shaped like a..."。注意 cigar 的拼写。
Speaker: Over the last five years scientists from thirteen countries have been taking part in the project and launching floats in their area of ocean patrol.
原文说 "Over the last five years... thirteen countries have been taking part"，而 "next year this number will rise to fourteen"。题目问的是 "so far"（迄今为止），所以选 13，不选 14。
到目前为止（so far），来自 13 个国家的科学家已经参与了这个项目。

analyses.content: Speaker: Each of the floats is dropped in the ocean from a boat at a set point and activated from a satellite.
图中对应步骤是 "Float dropped into ocean and [23]... by satellite"，原文明确说 "activated from a satellite"。
浮标被投放到海洋中后，会由卫星进行激活（activated）。
Speaker: During this time it's possible for it to cover quite large distances but the average is fifty kilometres.
图中 [24] 处标示的是虚线距离 "Average distance travelled"，原文直接对应 "the average is fifty kilometres"。
浮标在深海随洋流移动，尽管有时覆盖距离很远，但平均移动距离是 50 公里。
Speaker: ...it collects all sorts of data, most importantly variations in salinity, that's salt levels, and the changes in temperature, a bit like underwater weather balloons.
图中文字是 "Float records changes in salinity and [25]..."，原文对应 "variations in salinity... and the changes in temperature"。
浮标上升时记录数据，最重要的是记录盐度（salinity）的变化和温度（temperature）的变化。

analyses.content: 关于 El Nino（厄尔尼诺），浮标数据目前**已经（already）**在帮助确认其根本原因。
Speaker: For example, our understanding of the underlying causes of El Nino events is being confirmed by float data.
"Already helped" 和 "is being confirmed" 表示现在正在发生，对应 "At present"。
Speaker: Another way we're using float data is to help us to understand the mechanics of climate change... That's part of an ongoing variability study but the results are still a long way off.
"Results are still a long way off" 对应选项 C "In the long term future"。
关于 climate change（如全球变暖），这是持续变异研究的一部分，结果仍然路途遥远（a long way off）。
Speaker: ...we can advise the Navy on search and rescue missions. That's happening right now and many yachtsmen owe their lives to the success of this project.
"That's happening right now" 直接对应选项 A "At present"。
关于 naval rescues（海军救援），演讲者说这正在发生（happening right now），许多人因此获救。
Speaker: We hope it will help to bring about more sustainable fishing practices. We'll be seeing the results of that quite soon.
"Seeing the results of that quite soon" 对应选项 B "In the near future"。
关于 sustainable fishing practices（可持续捕鱼），演讲者说他们希望这能带来改变，并且**很快（quite soon）**就能看到结果。
Speaker: I agree that this concept is still a long way in the future, but it will come eventually and the float data will have made a contribution.
"Still a long way in the future" 直接对应选项 C "In the long term future"。
关于 crop selection（农作物选择/farmers planted appropriate grain），演讲者承认这个概念在未来还有很长的路要走（still a long way in the future）。
